title: Frozen non-evaluating JS literal subset parser: trailing commas plus Unicode code-point escapes

parent_v0_1.reason: After 296 historical trailing-comma removals, strict JSON localized a second source-valid JavaScript syntax feature: Unicode code-point escape syntax.

allowed_rule_1.name: TRAILING_COMMA_OUTSIDE_DOUBLE_QUOTED_STRINGS
allowed_rule_1.semantics: Omit a comma only when outside a double-quoted string and the next non-whitespace source character is ] or }.

allowed_rule_2.name: ACTIVE_JS_UNICODE_CODEPOINT_ESCAPE_INSIDE_DOUBLE_QUOTED_STRING
allowed_rule_2.admission: Code point must be <= U+10FFFF and must not be in U+D800..U+DFFF.
allowed_rule_2.parse_view_semantics: Replace the active JavaScript code-point escape with the corresponding literal Unicode scalar in the parse view. The original source string and bytes remain untouched and are represented by the transformation receipt.
allowed_rule_2.escaped_backslash_rule: A source sequence with an escaped/doubled backslash is not an active code-point escape and must not be transformed.

validation_canaries: Trailing commas in arrays and objects parse after omission.
Comma-before-bracket text inside a quoted string is unchanged.
Active \u{1076b} becomes exactly Unicode scalar U+1076B in the parse view.
A doubled-backslash literal representing text \u{1076b} remains textual rather than becoming U+1076B.
Invalid/out-of-range/surrogate code-point escapes remain unnormalized and fail closed.
An unsupported JavaScript identifier such as undefined remains unsupported and fails strict JSON.
Historical and current frozen lineara sources use the same implementation.
